label: rem:skein-coulomb-enhancement-interpretation
title: Magnitude, transition classes, and what the QOU predicts
html:
The leading-order half-life formula (hadron half-life) evaluates the Skein polynomial on the nucleus alone. It treats the emitted electron as a free particle. However, the electron trefoil T_{2,3} (electron knot) traverses the Coulomb field of Z protons as it exits the nucleus. Each electron-proton crossing carries a Skein weight. We evaluate the Skein polynomial on the full outgoing link T_{2,3} \cup \mathcal{N}(Z, N). This naturally generates the Coulomb enhancement.

We evaluate precisely the same Skein polynomial on the complete outgoing link rather than truncating at the weak vertex.

Magnitude. We average the integrated Coulomb enhancement over the electron energy spectrum. This yields a large, Z-dependent factor.

See Table: Skein-Coulomb enhancement factors.

These enhancements change decay rates by factors of 1.4 to 5. The leading-order predictions (verification) inherently include F_q through the nucleus-specific matrix element. The \sim 10--17\% residual in the verification table stems entirely from discrete nuclear structure effects. Shell closures, pairing, and deformation modify the Gamow--Teller strength \sigma_{\mathrm{GT}} at the individual-nucleus level.

Transition classes. The nuclear matrix element |\mathcal{M}_q|^2 varies by six orders of magnitude across the verification set. Measured \log ft values (NNDC/ENSDF) classify the transitions.

See Table: Beta-decay classification.

The QOU framework dictates the q-dependent modulation of each transition class via [2]_q, \tanh(\ln q), and \sigma_{\mathrm{GT}}. It does not predict the absolute matrix element from the leading-order Hecke computation alone. Predicting |\mathcal{M}_q|^2 for individual nuclei requires resolving the discrete shell structure. We must specify the precise quantum numbers of the parent and daughter nuclear states.

Predictions of the QOU. Within a single transition class of fixed \log ft, the QOU correctly predicts:

  1. The q-dependent scale: The factor (q + q^{-1})(q - q^{-1})^5 sets the overall decay-rate scale entirely from q.
  2. The A-dependence: We find t_{1/2} \propto A^{5/3} at fixed |\delta p| and fixed transition class.
  3. The q-sensitivity: We predict \partial \ln \Gamma / \partial \ln q \approx 48 without free parameters.
  4. The Coulomb enhancement structure: The term F_q(Z, E) emerges directly from the Skein crossing weights. This unifies the electromagnetic and weak interactions through the single deformation parameter q.
  5. The self-deformation: We observe a differential \Delta q_{\mathrm{eff}} correction induced by the hadron linking structure.
